capitals.name: Hulwan (Sar-e Pol-e Zahab)
capitals.note: The page gives no capital; "The founder ... governed in Hulwan". Principal settlements: Kermanshah, Hulwan, Dinavar, Shahrizor, Daquq, Daskara, Mandali, Numaniyah.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Annazid row): "The founder of the Annazids was Abu al-Fath Muhammad bin Annaz, who governed in Hulwan." He took Hulwan in 991. No area.
New keyframe: "By 1007: had expanded to Dinavar and Shapurkhast (Khorramabad)."
New keyframe: "In 1013, after Baha' al-Dawla's death, Abu al-Fath recaptured Shahrizor."

correction.text: Hulwan, Dinavar, Khorramabad, Shahrizor and the former Hasanwayhid lands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "the Annazid rule in the Jibal replaced that of the Hasanwayhids" after Badr's death in 1014. Kermanshah is left out: the Annazid page has them occupy it in 1014, lose it, and "retook Kermanshah ... from the Quhi Kurds" in 1039.
New keyframe: "1039: retook Kermanshah and the castles of Khulanjan and Aranba from the Quhi Kurds."

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: "1047: Muhalhil recaptured Kermanshah and Dinavar." The page also has the Seljuks overrunning Annazid lands in 1045-1047 and reinstating the Annazids as vassals in 1050 (not drawn), and mentions no Annazid land after 1055; the shape is held to 1116 as bridging.

ledger.note: 991: Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn Annaz takes Hulwan. 'The founder of the Annazids was Abu al-Fath Muhammad bin Annaz, who governed in Hulwan'; he took Hulwan in 991 and ruled until 1010 (infobox 990/991-1117).

by 1007: Dinavar and Shapurkhast. 'By 1007: had expanded to Dinavar and Shapurkhast (Khorramabad).' The page does not name the previous holder; Dinavar is the Hasanwayhid capital on the Hasanwayhid page, whose fighting with Abu al-Fath resumed in 1006-1007.
1013: Abu al-Fath recaptures Shahrizor. 'In 1013, after Baha' al-Dawla's death, Abu al-Fath recaptured Shahrizor.'

region.text: the former Hasanwayhid lands: Nahavand, Asadabad, Borujerd

ledger.note: 1015: the Annazids replace the Hasanwayhids in the Jibal. After Badr's death in 1014 'the Annazid rule in the Jibal replaced that of the Hasanwayhids'; the Annazid page itself does not mention 1015.
1039: the Annazids retake Kermanshah. '1039: retook Kermanshah and the castles of Khulanjan and Aranba from the Quhi Kurds.'
1040: Ala al-Dawla annexes Kermanshah and Dinavar. '1040: Alaa al-Dawla annexed Kermanshah and Dinavar' (read as the Kakuyid Ala al-Dawla Muhammad, 1008-1041).
1047: Muhalhil recaptures Kermanshah and Dinavar. '1047: Muhalhil recaptured Kermanshah and Dinavar.'

1117: the Annazids are said to have collapsed by 1117 (infobox disestablished 1117; 'Ibn al-Athir said they had been in power for 130 years by the time of Sorkhab bin Badr'). Sorkhab later governed Luristan under a Turkic governor and lost to the Khorshidi founder about 1174.

wars.name: Annazid-Hasanwayhid struggle for the Jibal
wars.outcome: Badr expelled Abu al-Fath ibn Annaz; hostilities resumed in 1006-1007; Abu al-Fath recaptured Shahrizor in 1013 and the Annazids replaced the Hasanwayhids in the Jibal after Badr's death in 1014.

wars.name: Annazid-Kakuyid war over Kermanshah and Dinavar
wars.outcome: Ala al-Dawla annexed Kermanshah and Dinavar in 1040; Muhalhil recaptured them in 1047.

wars.name: Seljuk overrun of the Annazids
wars.outcome: Tughril sent Ibrahim Yinal west in 1045 and the Annazid lands were overrun; Turkomans defeated Sa'adi and took Sirwan in 1047; in 1050 Tughril reinstated the Annazids as vassals with Muhalhil in Sirwan. No border drawn (the lands are not named).

certainty.note: A Kurdish emirate of fortress towns along the Zagros: Hulwan, Dinavar, Kermanshah, Shahrizor; no frontiers on the page. After 1055 the page names no Annazid land.

notes: Cliopatria has no Annazid row. Wikidata id not known; left null. The founder is Abu al-Fath Muhammad ibn Annaz (not Abu Shawk Faris, his son). The Annazid page does not mention Shahrizor 1013 or 1015 (both from the Hasanwayhid page), nor a capital; Hamadan is not Annazid on it. Conflicts: the Annazid page has them at Dinavar by 1007 and Kermanshah in 1014 while the Hasanwayhid page has Dinavar as the Hasanwayhid capital to 1015 (fighting resumed 1006-1007: both drawn, overlap 1007-1014 at Dinavar); the Kakuyid page has the Kakuyids taking Hulwan from the Annazids in 1023/24 and does not mention Kermanshah 1040/1047. The Seljuk entry 1045-1050 and the 1050 reinstatement as Seljuk vassals are not drawn (no land named; the vassalage belongs to the Seljuk dossier). 1055-1116: no Annazid land on the page; the 1047 shape is held as bridging to the infobox end. Counterparts: hasanwayhids and kakuyids (written here), buyid-dynasty (me-08-c), the Quhi Kurds (no dossier), the Khorshidi dynasty (Luristan, c. 1174; later). Gazetteer names needed: Hulwan, Dinavar, Shahrizor, Daquq, Daskara, Sirwan (drawn as coordinates or provinces).
